I actually remember these documented on the on the long-defunct [Sonic-CulT / X-CulT](https://info.sonicretro.org/Sonic_CulT) site, and their discovery can be traced [back to 2006](https://archive.ph/n9jLO) again by **BiggestSonicFan** on their forums. These are definitely less 'unfinished characters intended for the final game' and more... Well, you'll see.

First, there's two Sega AM2 staff members playable- Daichi Katagiri (FV co-coordinator) and Hiroshi Kataoka (FV director) of Sega AM2!

Their models are pretty basic so these were almost certainly snuck in as a joke.

[![Image 33: TIME TO SETTLE THIS, MR. NEEDLEMOUSE](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperssonictails.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperssonictailsb.png)
This is a bit more well-known though- the most famous hedgehog in the world and his fox buddy, Sonic & Tails!

 Maybe this screenshot looks a bit familiar to you- well, aside from me grabbing that specific one from The Cutting Room Floor, perhaps you saw something like it in a magazine back in the day? Thanks to some assistance from [SeventhForce](https://x.com/SeventhForce/status/1815404033185566954), UK magazine readers might remember it from [Computer & Video Games #174](https://archive.org/details/Computer_and_Video_Games_Issue_174_1996-05_EMAP_Images_GB/page/n25/mode/2up) covering Sonic the Fighters. [BiggestSonicFan](https://x.com/biggestsonicfan/status/1614750385218129920) helped out too and showed the real source of it, [Saturn Magazine 1996 #09](https://archive.org/details/sega-saturn-magazine-ja-1996-06-14) covering Fighting Vipers secrets- those cheeky gits at C&VG had nicked this shot then cropped out the Fighting Vipers characters, presenting it as if it was from Sonic the Fighters. Busted!
... Anyway, sorry, I had to get that squared away, that screenshot had been bothering me for years, so I'm glad other people knew what was up with it. _Anyway_, what are these two animals doing here? They're not Vipers! [As explained in a 1UP.com interview with Hiroshi Kataoka](https://segaretro.org/Interview:_Hiroshi_Kataoka_(2006-03-31)_by_1UP.com), Sonic and Tails were added into Fighting Vipers during the game's development as a joke, _possibly_ by Honey's character designer [Masahiro Sugiyama](https://segaretro.org/Masahiro_Sugiyama) although it's only mentioned as 'probably' being him rather than being definitively identified. Whoever was responsible was messing around with character models one day and put the pair in as a little goof (just filling up one character slot- Tails is the 2P palette) which was seen by Yu Suzuki, who then talked about it with Hiroshi Kataoka, who _then_ presented the idea of a Sonic fighting game to Sonic Team head and future insider trading criminal Yuji Naka, who loved the idea so much he approved it, eventually leading to Sonic the Fighters. We'll circle back around to Sonic the Fighters later, but that'll do for now.

Here's a full play through of the arcade game with Sonic, as recorded by [Tracker_TD](https://astromuseum.org/).

* * *

 Moving on, time to talk about the home versions of the game. There's not that many of them, but there's a lot to talk about here. 
![Image 34: I know what you're thinking, 'what does the teeny-tiny text under the Fighting Vipers logo on the box of the Saturn version read'? Well, you're in luck, it reads thus: 'THE ULTIMATE 3D FIGHTING ACTION. FIGHTINGVIPERS, the most innovative 3D fighting game is available at last! FIGHTINGVIPERS, even more exciting than another simulated fighting games! ULTRA REALISM, HYPER SPEED EXCITEMENT and THRILLS'. You're welcome, internet.

... Although y'know, you can see it for yourself on the scan of the filofax page from the PS2 game later on this website.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipers.png)

We must of course start with the Sega Saturn version, released in 1996 in all regions.

[![Image 35: Tokio getting his revenge for getting his ass kicked in the arcade section of this article.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand5.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand5.png)[![Image 36: AND HERE COMES RAXEL WITH THE GUITAR](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand2.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand2.png)[![Image 37: They can't have blood spray out in front of the Pepsi logo! Think of the lost sponsorship!](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand3.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand3.png)

 Given a fairly rapid home port (read any coverage of the game in British game mags at the time and they all breathlessly talked about how quick the conversion was), this was developed in-house by Sega AM2 themselves and brings the arcade game home quite faithfully, albeit with plenty of concessions. The Saturn was not 100% up to the task of one-to-one conversions of Model 2 games, but AM2's own ports show that you could make the hardware sing with a bit of effort, although this doesn't look quite as nice as their Virtua Fighter 2 port. Generally, the core of the game's been preserved with all the characters, moves and stages present and correct (the only major thing missing is the original attract mode demos, replaced with an FMV intro that includes [a few nods](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersomake7.png) to [Sonic the Fighters](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersomake8.png)!) but the character models are a lot less detailed (even less so than the VF2 port, plus broken armour pieces no longer stay in the arena) and the backgrounds are 2D images instead of 3D models but cleverly scaled and scrolled to make them look as 3D as possible. It _mostly_ keeps the rapid pace of the game too, although there is slight slowdown during things like armour breaks, wall smashes and pursuit attacks that give off too much of the pixellated blood effect. At least, in my experience on real hardware, anyway. The music has been redone too, taking advantage of the CD format to create more full-sounding songs with altered melodies (songs like UFO Diner / Occam's Razor and Armstone Town Night / Thirty-30 in particular benefit from the changes), plus a new song to go with the FMV intro, Vipers Venom. 
Where the Saturn version shines is in its extra features, which to this day aren't present in any other version. There's a few modes that were slowly becoming standards of home ports at the time, specifically Training to let you practice moves, a dedicated Vs. option with a streamlined character select screen and Team Battle to duke it out with teams of characters, as well as the less-common-at-the-time Playback that lets you record matches and watch them again later, plus watch exhibition matches from AM2 staff members and even famous VF players like Bunbunmaru! There's also two extra revisions of the core game, Arrange and Hyper, available in the options menu of all modes. As briefly explained in [Computer & Video Games](https://archive.org/details/Computer_and_Video_Games_Issue_180_1996-11_EMAP_Images_GB/page/n51/mode/2up?view=theater) of all places, Arrange is a rebalanced version of the arcade game with adjusted damage, armour and recovery values to make things a little fairer, while Hyper adds elements from Sonic the Fighters, specifically a sidestep with Back or Forward + P + K + G and a Hyper Mode done with Back + P + K that removes recovery from moves for the rest of that round (think the custom combos from Street Fighter Alpha 2) but leaves you without armour for the rest of the match. It's rare enough to see the home version rebalance the arcade game, but to include a bonus revision including over-the-top features from another game? Only on the Sega Saturn.

[![Image 38: Pepsiman says, ACHO!](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand6.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand6.png)[![Image 39: THEY'RE MAHLER AND MAHLER](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand4.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand4.png)[![Image 40: Tokio got cocky and said he was the main character of the game, Honey don't play that!](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand8.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersrand8.png) We're not done with extras though, as there's a whole bunch of silly unlockables to keep you playing, although the Japanese version has a couple of well-known exclusive extras. All versions have B.M. (the big boss), Mahler (the smaller boss) and Kumachan & Pandchan (the giant mascot statue seen in the Old Armstone Town stage) unlockable, with the Japanese version also having Aloha Honey (Honey with a ukelele), Uniform Honey (Honey in a school uniform) and Pepsiman (the only one who can quench your thirst) hidden too. There's also an extra set of options first unlocked by beating the game with any character with some further unlockables therein, including a portrait gallery (Japanese and European versions only!), Big Head Mode, a stage select for Arcade and more. You can learn more about these in our [special guide](https://gaminghell.co.uk/FightingVipersGuide.html) just for the Saturn version! These extras also get a little mention in [this Official Sega Saturn Magazine interview](https://archive.org/details/Official_Sega_Saturn_Magazine_013/page/n57/mode/2up?view=theater) with Hiroshi Kataoka about the conversion process which might be pretty interesting to read. 
One thing worth noting about the Saturn version is there's at least two revisions- listed as Rev. A and Rev. C online, we were alerted to the existence of an earlier revision by @GrimDark on Twitter, who mentioned that the first run of the Japanese version of Fighting Vipers was actually recalled due to a save glitch! According to their recollection, 'I experienced it 1st hand, system wouldn't save progress or high scores!' (he couldn't return his copy, living in the UK and all). We corroborated this with resident FV expert [@Zerochan](http://gaming.moe/) who confirmed something like this did happen, but was hazy on specifics. The only other lead we have is [this Japanese fansite](http://www.yk.rim.or.jp/~xevi/game/fv_ss.html) that explains the game wiped out _all_ of their save data on their Saturn's internal memory. _Ouch_. Unfortunately, that's all we have on this. If you have any more info, please get in touch at **themetalslug at gmail dot com**.

[![Image 41: Don't worry, this is the last time we see this specific title screen.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps2.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps2b.png)
We'd have to wait nine years for the next port, with 2005's Sega Ages 2500 Vol. 19: Fighting Vipers for the Playstation 2.

[![Image 42: LARGENESS OF BONCE](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps21.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps21b.png)[![Image 43: I had to find a way to get this pose from the intro in, I'm very predictable, I will not apologise.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps22.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps22b.png)[![Image 44: TRY! VIPER'S TEST](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps23.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps23b.png) This was at the middle point of the [Sega Ages 2500 series](https://kimimithegameeatingshemonster.com/sega-ages-2500-series-corner/), meaning they were at that in-between phase of after they were done remaking older games in 3D but before they got M2 to belt out some of the best-in-class retro compilations on the PS2. That doesn't mean this port is a slouch, far from it, and this is a very solid port. The [official website](https://web.archive.org/web/20060207160030/https://ages.sega.jp/fv/home.html) even touts that the Model 2 port work has been improved from Vol. 16: Virtua Fighter 2, particularly the lighting, and like that game this includes a 57.5 FPS option for something closer to the arcade game (although as [Kimimi points out](https://kimimithegameeatingshemonster.com/2023/05/12/sega-ages-2500-series-vol-19-fighting-vipers/)- and you should probably be reading that article instead- this is achieved with some wibbly technical stuff involving doubled-frames) so accuracy was indeed the aim. There's not much in the way of modes- Arcade, Ranking (as a separate menu option) and Vs. (now with a stage select rather than random stages), which means no Training, a real shame- but considering how rare accurate Model 2 ports were at this time (and still are, honestly), just having the arcade game at home, without any compromises as with the Saturn port, will be enough for the die-hard Vipers out there. 
While being an exacting port of the arcade version means all the extras from the Saturn port are gone (although the FMV intro music, Viper's Venom, is used in the Options menu), the _arcade_ extras are present and correct as listed earlier (as is the Pepsi advertising) with a few alterations to the unlock methods to make them a bit more manageable for home use. Instead of requiring 15,000 matches and an awkward code to play as Mahler, for example, you just need to play 150 or beat the arcade mode, and the famous skirt-destruction trick only needs 10 victories in a row instead of 100. The other changes methods are listed on our secrets chart page, but there's one new secret that, according to the official site, was originally only implemented in a one-night-only event in 1995 and not included in the released version, Kids Mode! Yes, that silly Big Head mode from the Saturn version was actually a reproduction of this one-off thing! It's about as goofy as it is in the Saturn version, but now in even higher fidelity. While somewhat rendered obsolete by the next version, the 57.5 FPS option remains exclusive to this port, so those who can play import PS2 games might want to still seek this version out.

[![Image 45: I won't lie, I really want that special edition Phantasy Star Generation:1 boxset just to keep all these filofax pages in one place.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperssegaagesfilofax1.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperssegaagesfilofax1b.png)[![Image 46: Let's play money making game~! We'll pay you to translate this! This is a serious offer!](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperssegaagesfilofax2.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperssegaagesfilofax2b.png) While we're here, enjoy these scans of the filofax _thing_ that came with this version.
We need to get it translated. Someday.

[![Image 47: See? This doesn't have the purple gradient. Different title screen.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps360.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps360b.png)
Next, a slightly shorter wait- just seven years this time- for 2012's Playstation 3 and Xbox 360 digital rerelease.

[![Image 48: GIANT SWING LET'S GOOOOOOOOO](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps3602.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps3602b.png)[![Image 49: Jane, shortly before giving Bahn a wet willy, flushing his head down the toilet and stuffing him into a locker.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps3601.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsps3601b.png)

 Part of a five-game line-up of Model 2 ports (Virtua Fighter 2 and Sonic the Fighters would be released worldwide, but Virtual On: Cyber Troopers and Virtua Striker would remain Japan-exclusive), this version of Fighting Vipers is somewhat similar to the Playstation 2 version in that it brings the arcade game home with some adjustments to its secrets to make them easier to unlock (in particular, Mahler is now available from the start) but also has the significant addition of online play, at long last. The netcode is _decent_ enough, certainly not a disaster like Street Fighter II': Hyper Fighting on Xbox Live Arcade but not best-in-class like the Code Mystics Neo Geo ports, it does the job. Otherwise, this is very much an arcade-accurate port, only missing the 57.5 FPS option from the PS2 release, everything else is in-tact. This does include regional differences though- the US and EU marketplaces versions are based on the USA / Export version of the arcade game, so Honey is Candy again and the Pepsi advertising has been removed, but the JP marketplaces have the Japanese version of the game, which means Pepsi for TV game _and_ Honey as Honey- [photos of](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipers360ps31kimimi1.jpg)[the Pepsi sponsorship](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipers360ps31kimimi2.jpg) provided by Ultra Powerful Pal of Gaming Hell, **Kimimi**.[![Image 50: HAHA I LIED THERE'S THE PURPLE GRADIENT AGAIN, GET OWNED NERD](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsjudgment1.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsjudgment1b.jpg)[![Image 51: bowling, get your bowling here](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsjudgment2.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersportsjudgment2b.jpg)
Finally for now, we go to that place where all Sega arcade ports live these days, I guess- the Yakuza / Like a Dragon series, or rather the spin-offs 2018's Judgment and 2021's Lost Judgment.

 Not a whole lot to be said here, but in [Judgment](https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/ps4/247615-judgment/faqs/77509/arcade-games) you'll find a set of Fighting Vipers cabs in the Club SEGA location on Nakamichi Street, and in [Lost Judgment](https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/ps4/320117-lost-judgment/faqs/79566/common-attractions) you'll still find them at that Club SEGA but also at the Sasaki Arcade on Tsurukame Alley in Ijincho's Commercial District, 100 Yen per play. You can also play it from the title screen as a versus minigame with a second player if you want! However, none of the secrets appear to work- no Mahler and certainly no Kids Mode, sorry. Additionally, both are based on the Japanese arcade version but, even in the Japanese versions of both games, the Pepsi advertising is no longer present. Would've been funny if they retroactively replaced it with one of the drinks brands present in the main Judgement games (a bit like how the Wii port of Gunblade N.Y. replaced some adverts with ones for Sonic and the Black Knight) but oh well. 

* * *

 Next, references to Fighting Vipers in other Sega games, although there's not that many!  Unlike Namco or Capcom who will throw any kind of reference to previous works in their games at the drop of a hat, Sega seems to work a little differently and crossovers with their games are a bit less common, with a lot of paperwork and back-and-forth involved in the process. A famous example in recent memory is [Joe Musashi being planned for Streets of Rage 4](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2020/05/streets_of_rage_4_dev_wanted_to_add_shinobis_joe_musashi_but_got_rejected_by_sega) but Sega not giving approval, and there was also [Steve Lycett on Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed](https://www.megavisions.net/interview-steve-lycett-on-sonic-all-stars-racing-transformed-10th-anniversary/) talking about how each character had to get the OK from the IP owner within Sega. It sounds complicated, and so it doesn't happen that often. Not to say it _never_ happens of course- the Super Monkey Ball games tend to get a lot of crossover stuff- but it's not all over the place like with Namco. Still, there are a few, so let's take a look... [![Image 52: Character selection screen from the arcade video game Sonic the Fighters featuring Amy Rose and Sonic the Hedgehog](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstf.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstfb.png)
... Starting, of course, with Sonic the Fighters. Told you we'd get back to it!

[![Image 53: I think Amy has a bootie bop too but they had to make sure Honey had one too, it's important.](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstf3.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstf3b.png)[![Image 54: oh my GOD honey has a GUN](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstf1.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstf1b.png)[![Image 55: 1PHoney vs. 2PHoney FIGHT](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstf2.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersstf2b.png) Back in 1996, Sonic the Fighters came out in arcades with eight playable characters and two non-playable bosses, but a few other characters were hiding in the code. Shortly after the release of Sonic Gems Collection on Playstation 2 and Gamecube in 2005, **BiggestSonicFan** found remnants of a completely unused character that had its model removed from the Gems Collection version and, upon exploring the arcade version and [documenting the findings on Sonic CulT / X-CulT](https://web.archive.org/web/20150725164539/http://forums.x-cult.org/topic/27-that-sonic-the-fighters-topic/), found what remained of Honey the Cat, a scrapped character based on Honey from Fighting Vipers but as a Sonic-style cat! That's years before we got Blaze the Cat, don't you know. The findings are also on [The Cutting Room Floor](https://tcrf.net/Sonic_Championship#Unplayable_Characters) alongside the other unused characters, also noting how Honey is mostly complete (many of her moves are taken from Knuckles but she has her traditional Bootie Bop from FV) but has some visual oddities- her eye-tracking is broken, her lower body turns into Amy's body when squished and she has no pre-match profile image. Despite these visual glitches, she's unique amongst the StF cast though as, while everyone else has a black-and-white clone, she has her 2P colours (blue clothes, blonde hair and pink fur) in mirror matches! Those who paid attention during the Saturn FV section might even recognise her 2P outfit here~
Honey's rediscovery many years after the game's release lead to an influx of interest and fanart of her, eventually being half-canonized into Sonic lore when the 2012 Playstation 3 and Xbox 360 port of Sonic the Fighters included a fixed-up version as a secret character (press Start over Amy's portrait on the Character Select screen- sadly, you can't play as her in Ranked matches) as well as appearances in both the Archie and IDW Sonic comics. However, as explained by Sonic series writer Ian Flynn in [Bumblecast Mini! for April 24th, 2024](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ObouKyc-vng) (at 6:23) found via [Sonic Wiki Zone](https://sonic.fandom.com/wiki/Honey_the_Cat), Honey is legally in a strange position and not particularly easy to include in other Sonic media or games because of how she's based on a Sega character from a different department of the company, which makes sense given what we know about crossover stuff within Sega.

 Next is 2002's Gamecube port of Beach Spikers, although this one's more related to the second Fighting Vipers. May as well leave it here, though! 
[GameFAQs](https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/arcade/566257-beach-spikers/cheats) lists some names you can enter in World Tour mode for extra customisation options, and one of them, FVIPERS...

[![Image 56: I mean, when else am I gonna get to mention Beach Spikers?](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersbeach1.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersbeach1.png)[![Image 57: SPONSORED BY PRINGLES](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersbeach2.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersbeach2.png)
... Unlocks some face, hair and uniform options based on Honey's look from Fighting Vipers 2. That's it.

Finally, we have 2012 / 2013's Project X Zone for the 3DS, which crosses over Namco, Capcom and Sega franchises, including Fighting Vipers.

Bahn shows up as a Solo Unit in [Chapter 2: The Fighting Vipers](https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/3ds/667255-project-x-zone/faqs/67352#section35) with Old Armstone Town as his theme song.

I don't have much else to add but the video above shows his interactions with the rest of the cast, some of which are pretty funny.

* * *

[![Image 58: FIGHTING VIPERS KIDS CONFIRMED???](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersbighead1.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersbighead1.png)[![Image 59: he is here... to bring you freshness](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperspepsiman2.jpg)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fviperspepsiman2.png) Of course, the main reason you're here is for our [Fighting Vipers guide](https://gaminghell.co.uk/FightingVipersGuide.html).
Produced _with love_, for _you_, this guide has [all the portrait pictures](https://gaminghell.co.uk/FightingVipersGallery.html) and [all the unlockables](https://gaminghell.co.uk/FightingVipersSecrets.html) including, characters, options and Japan-only stuff...

It's got almost everything you need to know about the hidden content in the Saturn port of Fighting Vipers. So read it. Whee!

* * *

[![Image 60: GAME OVER, YEAAAAAAAH!](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersgo.png)](https://gaminghell.co.uk/images/fvipers/fvipersgob.png)
And so ends our look at Fighting Vipers, one of the most ridiculous and _lovable_ video games of the 90s.

**[FIGHTING VIPERS WILL NEVER DIE. BLUE SKIES F-O-R-E-V-E-R](https://gaminghell.co.uk/index.html)**

****

7.title: Fighting Vipers
7.description: Fighting Vipers is a 3D Fighting Game series created by Sega's AM2 development team (of Virtua Fighter fame) in 1995. A sequel was released in 2001, and in the interim between the two games the casts of both FV and VF appeared in the Sega Saturn-only Fighters Megamix. Gameplay is similar to its...

_Fighting Vipers_ is a 3D [Fighting Game](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Fighting_Game "Fighting Game") series created by [Sega](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Sega "Sega")'s AM2 development team (of _[Virtua Fighter](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Virtua\_Fighter "Virtua Fighter")_ fame) in 1995. A sequel was released in 2001, and in the interim between the two games the [casts of both FV and VF appeared in the Sega Saturn-only](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Massive_Multiplayer_Crossover "Massive Multiplayer Crossover")[Fighters Megamix](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Fighters_Megamix "Fighters Megamix"). Gameplay is similar to its sister series, albeit faster, more forgiving in the control department, and has the addition of armor-breaking moves that soften up opponents and create weak points. Unlike _[Virtua Fighter](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Virtua\_Fighter "Virtua Fighter")_, arenas are walled, but the walls can be busted down if opponents are slammed against them enough times using the armor-break moves.

The story of the games involves armor-clad fighters run rampant in the metropolis, Armstone City. The dictator/mayor of Armstone City. Big Mahler, hosts a tournament for these fighters ending at the City Tower. The game's main character is Bahn, but Honey (Candy in the states) is the [Ensemble Darkhorse](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Ensemble_Darkhorse "Ensemble Darkhorse") and the only really well known character.

Currently, Fighting Vipers seems to have fallen into obscurity.

* * *

This series provide example of:

*   [Armor Is Useless](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Armor_Is_Useless "Armor Is Useless") (Subverted, the armor is useful, until it breaks off.)
*   [Ass Kicks You](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Ass_Kicks_You "Ass Kicks You") (Many of Honey's moves use her posterior as a weapon.) 
    *   Sanman has two or three as well.

*   [Bishonen](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Bishonen "Bishonen") (Tokio)
*   [Bonus Boss](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Bonus_Boss "Bonus Boss") (Kuhn)
*   [Bowdlerization](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Bowdlerization "Bowdlerization"): Sega of America removed a wallpaper from the home port of the game featuring Honey stripped down to her undergarments (basically, what you see when you break all her armor.)
*   [Break Meter](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Break_Meter "Break Meter"): Characters have specific moves that damage armor. This was transferred to _[Fighters Megamix](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Fighters\_Megamix "Fighters Megamix")_, where the _[Virtua Fighter](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Virtua\_Fighter "Virtua Fighter")_ characters' signature moves were given this property.
*   [Chained by Fashion](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Chained_by_Fashion "Chained by Fashion"): Raxel's armor makes heavy use of chains for whatever reason.
*   [Clothing Damage](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Clothing_Damage "Clothing Damage") (The breakable armor.)
*   [Crossover](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Crossover "Crossover") (_[Fighters Megamix](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Fighters\_Megamix "Fighters Megamix")_ which featured characters from its sister games _[Virtua Fighter](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Virtua\_Fighter "Virtua Fighter")_, _[Sonic The Fighters](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Sonic\_the\_Hedgehog "Sonic the Hedgehog")_, _[Virtua Cop](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Virtua\_Cop "Virtua Cop")_ and _[Daytona USA](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Daytona\_USA "Daytona USA")_)
*   [Cultural Translation](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Cultural_Translation "Cultural Translation"): In the American release of the first game, Honey dyed her hair blond and was renamed Candy.
*   [The Cutie](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/The_Cutie "The Cutie") (Emi)
*   [Dummied Out](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Dummied_Out "Dummied Out")[(Sonic, Tails and Takashi Iizuka)](http://www.x-cult.org/games/150/Fighting_Vipers)
*   [Expy](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Expy "Expy") (Bahn is essentially [Jotaro Kujo.](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/JoJo%27s_Bizarre_Adventure "JoJo's Bizarre Adventure"))
*   [Fad Super](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Fad_Super "Fad Super") (Grace, Picky, and Charlie are based on extreme sports--rollerblading, skateboarding, and BMX, respectively.)
*   [Genki Girl](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Genki_Girl "Genki Girl") (Emi)
*   [Guest Fighter](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Guest_Fighter "Guest Fighter") (PEPSIMAN!!) 
    *   Through hacking, [Sonic and Tails](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Sonic_the_Hedgehog "Sonic the Hedgehog")

*   [I Know Madden Kombat](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/I_Know_Madden_Kombat "I Know Madden Kombat") (Picky and Charlie. Sanman's throw is a bowling toss — there's even a pin-hitting sound effect.)
*   [Improbable Weapon User](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Improbable_Weapon_User "Improbable Weapon User") (Speaking of Picky and Charlie... Especially Charlie; very few people not named [Jackie Chan](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Jackie_Chan "Jackie Chan") beat guys up with bicycles.)
*   [Instrument of Murder](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Instrument_of_Murder "Instrument of Murder") (Raxel's guitar)
*   [Joke Character](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Joke_Character "Joke Character") (Kumachan)
*   [Lawyer-Friendly Cameo](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Lawyer-Friendly_Cameo "Lawyer-Friendly Cameo") (Jane in the American release doesn't look like much due to [Palette Swap](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Palette_Swap "Palette Swap"). In the original Japanese versions however, she turns out to be [Private Vasquez](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Aliens "Aliens").)
*   [Mighty Glacier](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Mighty_Glacier "Mighty Glacier") (Sanman)
*   [Ms. Fanservice](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Ms._Fanservice "Ms. Fanservice") Honey. Generally she is the only thing people remember about the series.
*   [No Guy Wants an Amazon](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/No_Guy_Wants_an_Amazon "No Guy Wants an Amazon") (Grace's backstory)
*   [Palette Swap](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Palette_Swap "Palette Swap") (Jane in the American version.)
*   [Product Placement](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Product_Placement "Product Placement") (Pepsiman and Picky's Pepsi skateboard in the first game.)
*   [Rollerblade Good](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Rollerblade_Good "Rollerblade Good") (Grace)
*   [SNK Boss](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/SNK_Boss "SNK Boss") (Kuhn. OUCH. And when he beats you, you don't get another go at him.)
*   [Stripperiffic](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Stripperiffic "Stripperiffic") (Grace and ~~ Candy~~ Honey wear next to nothing when their armor breaks off.)
*   [Totally Radical](https://tropedia.fandom.com/wiki/Totally_Radical "Totally Radical") (seems to be what AM 2 was going for when they made the game)

A delightful piece of archival footage has surfaced on YouTube, which shows Japanese cosplayers battling it out in a 1995 tournament on Sega’s _Fighting Vipers._ The footage appears as part of a Japanese gaming show, and was uploaded to YouTube this week by user [“Kukun Kun”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WGxgaNE1iF0&t=595s). before being spotted by the eagle-eye of history lover [John Andersen](https://twitter.com/JohnAndersen21/status/1390450769715924995?s=20).

The brief feature, shot at the [Sega GIGO center in Roppongi, Tokyo](https://segaretro.org/Roppongi_GiGO), sees various players competing on what was then Sega’s hottest release. Despite _Fighting Vipers_‘ varied and over-the-top cast of characters, it appears that almost everyone participating here has chosen to don the battle armor of cutesy femme Honey (or “Candy” in the international release).

I was super stoked to catch a fleeting glimpse of one woman who had chosen to cosplay my favorite character, Jane, but for the most part it’s quite clear who is _Fighting Vipers_ breakout superstar… Oh, I don’t mean Honey… I’m talkin’ ’bout the Bad Boy rocking the obligatory leather jacket and ’90s “wet look”. Boy, we drowned ourselves in hair gel in those days. I hope he’s still playing fighting games.

Elsewhere in the episode, one can find footage of players queuing up to purchase _Dragon Quest VI on the Super Famicom,_ a brief preview of _Street Fighter Alpha 2_, and footage of a group of middle-aged adults having a _Virtua Fighter 2_ house party… what is what I call Saturday night even in 2021.

Thanks to Kukun Kun for sharing this wonderful blast from the past.

Honey
-----

[![Image 3: Stub-image](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/sega/images/0/0b/Stub-image.png/revision/latest?cb=20240422165611)](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Help:Stub "Help:Stub")
**Honey/Candy** is a fictional character from the video game series _[Fighting Vipers](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Fighting\_Vipers "Fighting Vipers")_. She was renamed "Candy" in the North American and PAL localization of _Fighting Vipers_. She also reappears as a playable character in _[Fighting Vipers 2](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Fighting\_Vipers\_2 "Fighting Vipers 2")_, where her name was changed back to Honey for the PAL release.

*   [1 History](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#History)
    *   [1.1 Fighting Vipers](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Fighting_Vipers)
    *   [1.2 Fighting Vipers 2](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Fighting_Vipers_2)
    *   [1.3 Sonic the Fighters](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Sonic_the_Fighters)

*   [2 International Release Reference](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#International_Release_Reference)
*   [3 Trivia](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Trivia)
*   [4 Gallery](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Gallery)

History[](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#History "Link to this header")[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsega.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHoney%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D1&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Fighting Vipers[](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Fighting_Vipers "Link to this header")[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsega.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHoney%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

Honey/Candy is a girl who dreams of becoming an apparel designer. Learning of the Viper Tournaments, she dons her own self made rubber armor, and enters, heartily feeling it would be a great idea to use the tournament to show off her latest works and styles.

### Fighting Vipers 2[](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Fighting_Vipers_2 "Link to this header")[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsega.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHoney%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D3&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

Even if B.M. would order a crackdown on Vipers, that would not stop her dreams either! Honey/Candy feels that even the Viper Hunts would be as great as an opportunity as the last tournament held two years ago to show her styles.

### Sonic the Fighters[](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#Sonic_the_Fighters "Link to this header")[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsega.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHoney%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D4&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]

[Honey the Cat](https://sonic.fandom.com/wiki/Honey_the_Cat) was an unused character whose design and name are heavily based on Honey as she appears in Fighting Vipers. Her data was leftover in Sonic the Fighters, originally found via hacking. She was later added back into the game officially as part of the 2012 HD re-releases of the game.

International Release Reference[](https://sega.fandom.com/wiki/Honey#International_Release_Reference "Link to this header")[[](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fsega.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FHoney%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D5&uselang=en "Sign in to edit")]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In all versions of _Fighting Vipers_, her home stage Bayside contains graffiti that reads, "**In Memory of Honey you will always be rememberd by your family and friends R.I.P**", which would indicate that Honey is dead, however it may be in reference to the International releases of the game changing her name from Honey to Candy, causing the "death" of the Honey name. Despite this she would continue to be known as **Honey** in every appearance in **Japan.** Her original name would also eventually be restored in the **PAL** release of _Fighting Vipers 2_.
